policy_presence.summary: Retained public Claims show scoped institutional material. Currentness and complete policy coverage remain PARTIAL.

ai_disclosure.summary: Teacher guidance asks staff to remind students to disclose help and sources honestly; templates address when AI use must be accounted for. Apply the relevant course’s actual requirements.

coursework.summary: KTH student guidance says the teacher’s course-specific rule takes precedence. Four common approaches describe possible course policies, not permission for every assignment.

exams.summary: The retained student record covers graded assignments and exams under course-specific instructions. Service access and general guidance cannot override the exam’s rules.

privacy_data_entry.summary: Staff guidance advises removing personal data, while legal guidance requires examining GDPR, storage, third-party and training conditions. Copilot guidance still excludes personal, sensitive or confidential material.

academic_integrity.summary: Course templates retain student responsibility for submitted work and warn of disciplinary action for unauthorised AI use. No specific hearing procedure, sanction or appeal deadline is established here.

approved_tools.summary: A retained record describes employee-accessible Copilot Chat with a KTH account. It does not establish student entitlement; separate service records remain pending eligibility review and do not permit assessed use.

named_ai_services.summary: Named services in retained Claims are discovery context only; eligibility and assessment permission remain unverified.

teaching_guidance.summary: Teachers are asked to consider how AI affects learning and write course-specific acceptable-use information. The excluded Faculty Council wording is not recast here as a binding university-wide mandate.

research_guidance.summary: No retained public Claim establishes a specific KTH research-publication or authorship rule in this view. Course and staff guidance should not be expanded into such a rule.

security_procurement.summary: Employee recommendations call for checking duties, rules, agreements and ethical consequences before sharing information. Legal-data checks remain separate from course assessment permission.
